questions.question: [Media Language] Q: What is the difference between denotation and connotation?
questions.correctAnswer: Denotation is the literal, surface-level meaning of a sign — what you actually see (e.g. a red rose is a flower). Connotation is the deeper cultural meaning it suggests (e.g. a red rose connotes love, passion, romance).
questions.explanation: Denotation is the literal, surface-level meaning of a sign — what you actually see (e.g. a red rose is a flower). Connotation is the deeper cultural meaning it suggests (e.g. a red rose connotes love, passion, romance).

questions.question: [Media Language] Q: Explain the three types of technical codes used in film and television.
questions.correctAnswer: Camerawork: shot types (close-up, wide shot, low angle) and movement that frame the action. Editing: cuts, transitions, pace and rhythm that shape narrative and emotion. Sound: diegetic (within the world) and non-diegetic (added) sound that creates atmosphere and meaning.
questions.explanation: Camerawork: shot types (close-up, wide shot, low angle) and movement that frame the action. Editing: cuts, transitions, pace and rhythm that shape narrative and emotion. Sound: diegetic (within the world) and non-diegetic (added) sound that creates atmosphere and meaning.

questions.question: [Media Language] Q: What is intertextuality and why do media producers use it?
questions.correctAnswer: Intertextuality is when one media product references or borrows from another — e.g. The Simpsons parodying a film scene. Producers use it to create humour, show sophistication, appeal to knowledgeable audiences, and add layers of meaning.
questions.explanation: Intertextuality is when one media product references or borrows from another — e.g. The Simpsons parodying a film scene. Producers use it to create humour, show sophistication, appeal to knowledgeable audiences, and add layers of meaning.

questions.question: [Online, Social & Participatory Media] Q: What is the 'prosumer' and how has digital media created this role?
questions.correctAnswer: A prosumer is someone who both produces and consumes media content. Digital media — smartphones, social media platforms, editing apps — has enabled audiences to create and share content, not just passively consume it. Examples include YouTube vloggers, TikTok creators, and fan fiction writers.

questions.question: [Online, Social & Participatory Media] Q: How do algorithms affect what audiences see on social media?
questions.correctAnswer: Algorithms analyse user behaviour (likes, shares, watch time) to personalise content feeds. They prioritise content likely to generate engagement, creating filter bubbles where users see posts that reinforce their existing views. This can polarise opinions and limit exposure to diverse perspectives.
